Order 
This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in relation to Crime No.128/2025 registered at Police Station Ranjhi, District Jabalpur for the offence punishable under Section 376 and 376(2)(n) of the IPC.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant came in contact with the prosecutrix in 2014 and thereafter the applicant and prosecutrix were in relationship till 20.06.2024 and they were in physical relation but the report was made to the police on 20.02.2025 on the ground that the applicant has developed physical relation with the prosecutrix on the false pretext of marriage and now he has refused to enter into marriage with her, therefore, the offence has been registered.

Learned counsel further NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12740 2 MCRC-10952-2025 submits that it is clear that the incident is of 2014 and the prosecutrix was major at the relevant point of time and she was a consenting party and for almost 10 years, they were in relationship but when marriage could not be solmenized for some reason and engagement of the present applicant was settled with some other girl, then the report was made to the police by the prosecutrix.

He further submits that the present applicant is a government employee and if he is arrested in such a Lakhan Lal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148250384/
1 false case, his whole service career would be ruined as such, the present applicant is entitled to get the benefit of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, the counsel for the State has opposed the submissions made by the counsel for the applicant, read over the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and submits that when prosecutrix is alleging that is it is a case wherein physical relation was developed after giving false assurance of marriage, therefore, the offence is rightly made out and bail application deserves to be rejected.
5. Learned counsel for the objector has also submitted that prosecutrix was willing to get married with the applicant but the applicant declined the same.
He submits that the video chats between both the parties are available on record, however, they are not the complete chats.

He submits that relationship was developed by the applicant on the false assurance of marriage and now the applicant is refusing to enter into marriage with the prosecutrix, therefore, the bail application deserves to be rejected.

6. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case-diary and the allegation made against the present applicant, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12740 3 MCRC-10952-2025 which prima facie gives an impression that both of them were consenting party.

I am inclined to grant interim protection to the present applicant as both the prosecutrix and applicant are major and were in relationship since 2014 which continued upto 2024, therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer/Arresting Officer of the Police Station concerned.
7. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 482(2) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE PK Lakhan Lal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148250384/
